alternatives.name: Light ice cream, smaller portion (store-bought step down)
alternatives.why: A step down, not a free food. On the walmart.com labels (2026-10-18), Great Value regular vanilla shows 11 g added sugar and 5 g saturated fat per 2/3 cup, Halo Top shows 4 g added sugar and 1 g saturated fat, and Breyers Light shows 14 g added sugar and 3 g saturated fat. So 'light' does not always mean less sugar: read the label. Halo Top gets its low sugar partly from sugar alcohols and is still an ultra-processed (NOVA 4) product. DGA 2025-2030 advises limiting both added sugars and non-nutritive sweeteners. Light ice cream stays a 'limit' food counted in the sweets allowance (Bach-Faig 2011: sweets ≤2 servings/week).
alternatives.lookFor: Lowest added sugar per serving (AHA: ≤36 g added sugar per day for men; FDA: 5% DV or less is low); lower saturated fat; a short ingredient list; stick to the label serving (2/3 cup) or less, in a small bowl. If the label lists sugar alcohols (erythritol, sorbitol, maltitol), large amounts can upset the stomach. On the Nutrition Facts label, 5% DV or less of sodium/added sugars per serving is low and 20% DV or more is high (FDA).

alternatives.name: Banana-mango 'nice cream' with Greek yogurt
alternatives.why: Blend frozen banana and/or mango with plain Greek yogurt until it is thick and soft-serve-like (add a spoon of milk or water if the blender sticks). The fruit gives the sweetness, the yogurt adds protein, and nothing is ultra-processed (Hall 2019 found ~500 kcal/day more eaten on an ultra-processed diet). Vanilla is optional. Honey is optional and counts as added sugar (WHO free sugars; AHA ≤36 g/day for men), so leave it out if the fruit is ripe enough. No fresh bananas frozen yet? Use the Great Value frozen sliced bananas, or slice ripe fresh bananas and freeze them in a bag (about 2 hours or overnight).
alternatives.lookFor: Frozen fruit with fruit as the only ingredient (0 g added sugars); plain Greek yogurt (milk + cultures).
